newsitem.title: USA: Wall St stocks seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall St stocks seen opening higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to head higher at the opening, following through on Friday's late rally.
Analysts said the market would draw its strength in early trading from rallies in European and Asian markets, a steady dollar, and a slight improvement in the bond market.

"It looks as though the rally will probably continue," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "We have a steady bond market and a steady dollar so we will probably have a steady opening."
But Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said the start was no indication of how the market would finish. A reversal is possible during the day, he said.
"I imagine we'll open on a firm note. But the thing about volatile markets with huge swings is that the open is no key as to how the market will close," he said.
Cardillo said stocks were trading at perilously high levels and that a correction would be normal.
"Any time soon we could see a pullback of at least five percent," he said. "The market is setting itself up for some kind of reversal."
Among special situations that investors will be keeping an eye on is Tyco International Ltd's offer to acquire American Standard Cos Inc.
The Wall Street Journal reported that Tyco last month proposed buying American Standard for $50 a share in stock and cash, or about $4 billion plus assumption of debt.
"I don't know if this deal will have an influence on the overall market. But the market has benefited from the enormous deals of last year," Wachtel said.
In Tokyo the Nikkei Average rose 4.7 percent to 18,118.79, its first rally in a week.
In London the FTSE 100 Index was up 41 points at 4097.
Among U.S. shares traded in London, General Motors Corp was up 1/4 at 61-3/8, and International Business Machines Corp was down 1/4 at 162-3/4.
The dollar was stalled in Tokyo and within a narrow range in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were thinly mixed, with the long bond up 1/32 to yield 6.84 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's "Heard on the Street" column said the more than 20 percent gains in stock market indices over the past year look impressive, but closer examination reveals that a lot of the gains were generated by a small group of stocks with enormous market value whose strong performance overshadowed more ordinary returns of the majority of issues.
